samples.summary: New emitter of a parsed-form-validated URL: the href string is now written verbatim into visible document text without the `hasUrlAlteringChars` pairing that core's `isSafeUrl` contract requires of emitters
samples.evidence: `normalizeLinkUrl` (packages/docs/src/view/url-detect.ts:9-19) validates `new URL(trimmed).protocol` but returns the *raw* trimmed input, not the parsed serialization. `packages/core/src/url/index.ts:55` states: "Callers that go on to *emit* the string they validated must pair this with `hasUrlAlteringChars`" — and markdown.ts:328 / pdf-painter.ts:903 do exactly that. The diff adds a new emitter that does not: editor.ts:3647 and text-box-editor.ts:1218 insert that raw string as visible document *text*, and the rewrite is triggered precisely when text === href, i.e. the case where the user reads the rendered text as the destination. A URL accepted by normalizeLinkUrl may contain tab/CR/LF or C0/C1 characters (the WHATWG parser deletes or trims them before reading the scheme, so `isSafeUrl` sees a different string than the one now displayed), producing a rendered "URL" that is not the URL a click resolves. I could not build a privilege-crossing exploit: the string is supplied by the local user in the popover input, not by a collaborator or a pasted document, and the collaborator-controlled old href is only compared for equality (linkTextFollowsHref, link-run.ts:67) and never re-emitted. Protocol escalation is blocked — I tested `javascript:alert(1)`, `ja\tvascript:...` and `javascript\n:...` against the scheme regex plus `isSafeUrl` and all are rejected or normalize to https. Impact is therefore limited to self-inflicted display/target confusion, hence minor. Fix would be to reject `hasUrlAlteringChars(url)` in `normalizeLinkUrl`, which also protects the pre-existing href emitters.
searchedFor: Grep 'insertLink' over packages/{frontend,docs}/src to enumerate all callers
